about.title: Moraga Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Moraga is a small, close-knit Contra Costa County community, and most residents drive out of town for hospital care or specialist treatment. That doesn't change the legal footing when something goes wrong during a procedure, a delayed diagnosis, or a hospital stay. California handles medical malpractice differently than a typical injury claim — the MICRA law sets a shorter filing window, requires a 90-day notice before a lawsuit, caps non-economic damages (with the cap rising each year), and almost always requires a qualified medical expert to support the claim. These rules make early legal guidance especially important, since a missed deadline can end a case before it starts. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly — we connect Moraga residents with an independent, contingency-fee attorney who can review medical records, assess whether the standard of care was met, and explain what MICRA means for your specific timeline. There's no cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why MICRA Rules Make Timing Critical

items.title: Notice Comes Before the Clock Runs Out
items.desc: California requires a 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider before a malpractice lawsuit can be filed. Missing this step can delay or derail a claim, so early attorney review matters.

items.title: The Filing Window Is Short and Firm
items.desc: Claims generally must be filed within one year of discovering the harm, and no later than three years from the injury itself. An attorney can help pinpoint where you stand on that timeline.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: A qualified medical expert typically has to confirm the standard of care was violated. The attorney network LawProactive connects you with can help arrange that kind of review.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law requires showing the provider fell below the accepted standard of care, not just that the result was disappointing or unexpected. An independent attorney can review your records to see whether that standard was actually met.

items.question: Where would a Moraga malpractice case typically be filed?
items.answer: Since Moraga is in Contra Costa County, most claims connected to care received here or nearby would generally be filed in Contra Costa County courts, though venue can depend on where the provider or facility is located. An attorney can confirm the right court for your situation.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and the attorneys in the network work on contingency — meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
